covalent.note: Covalent radius; PubChem's values are those of Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832.

vdw.note: Van der Waals radius (Los Alamos National Laboratory).

allen.note: Configuration energy (Allen electronegativity) in eV, not converted to the Pauling-like scale; Mann 2000b.

crust.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for Earth's crust, via PubChem ('5.65×10³ milligrams per kilogram').

ocean.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for sea water, via PubChem ('1×10⁻³ milligrams per liter').

solar.note: Proto-solar (4.567 Ga ago) elemental mass fraction, column 'Elemental Mass Fractions' of ESM Table A13; the table gives no uncertainty (relative sigma of N(E) in Table 6 applies).

solarLogEps.note: A(E) = log10(N_E/N_H) + 12, 'Solar System Present' log (E/H)+12; basis: meteoritic (CI-chondrite) value; unc = 1 sigma in dex as printed.

body.note: Our table from ICRP Publication 23 has no amount for this element in the reference body (tools/curated/abundance.toml lists what was left out and why).

temperature.note: The COD entry does not state the temperature of the measurement.

crystal.reference: Wyckoff, R. W. G. (1963). Crystal Structures 1, 7.
crystal.note: Wyckoff's compilation (no primary reference in CIF); temperature not stated. COD 9017383 (natural titanium mineral) lists the same cell.

production.basis: mine production, ilmenite and rutile, TiO2 content

tonnesPerYear.note: World mine production, ilmenite and rutile, TiO2 content, 2025 (USGS: 9,800 thousand metric tons).

unitValue.note: Price, dollars per kilogram [Titanium sponge metal], 2025; per kg of the material named, as USGS gives it.

critical.note: Titanium metal only; the 2023 study assessed 'titanium' (minerals) and 'titanium metal' separately, and only titanium metal is critical.

origin.note: Read off Fig. 39 at the dotted 'age of the Sun' line (t = 9.2 Gyr after the Big Bang, 4.6 Gyr ago): pixel fractions of the stacked areas (agb 0.079, massive_stars 0.537, white_dwarfs 0.384); quantised to 0.05. Stack height 43 px. Paper: 'For the elements from Ne to Ge, the newly synthesized amounts are very small for AGB stars, and the small green areas are mostly for mass loss.' Paper: 'K, Sc, V and Ti are known to be under-produced at all metallicity ranges in theoretical models with respect to the observations' and 'The under-production of the elements around Ti is a long-standing problem.'

biology.note: Not known to be essential for plants or for humans.

history.nameOrigin: Named by Klaproth after the Titans, the giant children of Earth and Sky in Greek myth.
history.note: Gregor found it in a Cornish mineral and called it menachanite; Klaproth rediscovered and named it in 1795. Nilson and Pettersson made impure metal in 1887; Hunter made the first pure metal by heating the tetrachloride with sodium.

prose.text: Titanium is a transition metal as strong as many steels but much lighter, and it shrugs off seawater and body fluids; we meet it in aircraft, spectacle frames and hip implants, onto which living bone grows firmly. Surprisingly, most mined titanium never becomes metal at all: it is turned into titanium dioxide, the brilliant white pigment in paint, paper and sunscreen. Radioactive titanium-44, with a half-life of about 59 years, is forged in exploding stars, and its gamma rays have been detected from young supernova remnants. The atom, [Ar] 3d² 4s², has two unpaired 3d electrons and the ground term ³F₂.
